records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:31 — [confidence 100, P2] `return namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent` gives the same denial key to `(name="dash_a", parent="b")` and `(name="dash", parent="a_b")`, so denying the former suppresses an explicitly permitted request for the latter for 30 seconds because Check returns before evaluating its permissions; the strongest rebuttal is that callers supply valid resource identifiers, but underscore-containing identifiers are not rejected by validateCheckRequest and tuple encoding is still ambiguous.
records.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a cache key collision vulnerability. Looking at the diff, line 31 in cache.go shows: `return namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent`. This concatenation with underscores as separators creates ambiguity when any of the components contain underscores. For example, (name='dash_a', parent='b') produces the same key as (name='dash', parent='a_b').
